claims.text: Tailored phase-selective recrystallization can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an example of the target eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast target alloy has a lamellar microstructure consisting of alternating soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
A controlled heat treatment can selectively recrystallize the soft FCC phase without substantially altering the hard phase.
Cryo-rolling may be used before the selective-recrystallization heat treatment.
Phase-selective recrystallization creates a dual-scale hierarchical microstructure.
The required processing window is likely at intermediate temperatures below those causing full recrystallization of the B2 phase.
The resulting microstructure contains a recrystallized soft phase embedded within a preserved hard-phase skeleton or lamellar network.
The selectively recrystallized soft phase is fine-grained.
The hierarchical soft-phase/hard-phase architecture promotes effective strain partitioning.
Selective recrystallization of the soft phase increases strain-hardening capacity and ductility.
The contiguous hard-phase skeleton sustains high strength through load transfer.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 25% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy can reach about 35% uniform elongation.
The approximately 35% uniform elongation represents an increase relative to the as-cast baseline.
As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys have coarse lamellae and a limited combination of strength and ductility.
Over-annealing or recrystallizing both phases may eliminate the beneficial dual-phase synergy.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is defined relative to an as-cast baseline, but the experiment includes only selectively recrystallized and fully annealed sets, and the falsification rule compares those two treatments rather than testing against an untreated as-cast control.
